name: Knowledge-gap reduction
question: Which objects, if observed now, would most reduce what we do not know: missing expected evidence, drifting ephemerides, stale or uncertain records, empty sky?

features.name: coverage_gap_fraction
features.rationale: Missing evidence that the object's kind is expected to have is the most direct blank space.

features.name: ephemeris_drift
features.rationale: When the predicted transit-time uncertainty approaches the transit duration, one timed observation restores predictability for years.

features.name: evidence_staleness
features.rationale: Old measurements may no longer describe the object.

features.name: classification_uncertainty
features.rationale: A catalogue's own uncertainty flag marks a semantic edge worth resolving.

features.name: region_coverage
features.rationale: Empty regions of sky are blank spaces by construction.

features.name: visibility
features.rationale: Only observable ignorance can be reduced tonight.
